To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mice which have been previously exposed to stress are protected against the physiological alterations elicited by more severe stress, and that this tolerance is related to an accelerated turnover of brain dopamine.
exposure to stress prior to a more severe stress results in a tolerance to the effects of the more severe stress.
tolerance to stress is associated with increased brain dopamine turnover.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a single stressor (a revolving drum) on the behavioral and neurochemical response of mice to subsequent stress.
the effects of stress on the brain and its relationship to the dopaminergic system.
the relationship between stress and dopamine metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tolerance to stress is related to a rapid turnover rate of brain dopamine.
stress-tolerance is associated with a more rapid rate of turnover of brain dopamine.
stress-tolerance is related to an increased turnover rate of dopamine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tolerance to stress is associated with an increased turnover of dopamine.
stress tolerance is associated with an increase in dopamine turnover.
the stress-induced increase in dopamine turnover may be an essential component of the stress response and that tolerance to stress may be related to the rate of dopamine turnover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of a stressor are not only dependent on the nature of the stressor itself, but also on the individual’s prior exposure to stress.
tolerance to stress is a function of the brain’s dopaminergic system.
stress tolerance is a state of increased dopamine turnover, which may be induced by prior stress and may be reversed by inhibition of catecholamine synthesis.
